story_text:
[画像: BECOME A DEALER. Run a shop? The Kickstarter five-unit carton gets you started. Take more if you like. Apply.]
## Meet Rainy 75 V2
[画像: EVERYTHING CHANGED. THE KEY DIDN'T. Washington, 1963. Lunar orbit, 1969. Your desk, now. The machines kept changing. The key under your finger never did.]
[画像: A MILLION DESKS. Rainy 75, 2024: 1,100,000+ sold worldwide. It started as a Kickstarter. It ended up on desks on every continent. Then we rebuilt every part.]
## What's New
[画像: TORN DOWN. REBUILT. Bigger battery, magnetic back, solid CNC aluminum. We took the old one apart and put it back together faster, slimmer, tool-free.]
[画像: Rainy 75 V2 upgrades. Key upgrades: tool-free quick-release case with ball-catch closure; 8 kHz polling (was 1 kHz), 0.08 ms on every key; swappable top-right modules (knob in the box, color screen and matrix display + knob as add-ons); magnetic detachable rear plate; 17.4 mm front height with an 8.5° typing angle. Also in V2: six acoustic layers, a sculpted three-curve waistline, 10,000 mAh on every model, an outside power switch, a 2.4G receiver stored inside, Deep or Crisp sound, three gasket mounts (socks, bean, sleeve), tuned stabilizers, the WOBKEY Studio web driver with VIA support, and twelve variants in eight colorways.]
## Battery, 8K & Low Front
[画像: DILEMMA. DILEMMA. DILEMMA. Three of them, two years, solved. Big battery or low front. Fast or long-lived. Bright or cheap. Yes.]
[画像: 8,000 Hz. 10,000 mAh. 17.4 mm. At once. Up to 1000 hours before you reach for a cable.]
Keyboards make you choose. A big battery means a thick case. Speed means charging every few days. Lights mean a higher price. You pick one and give up the other.
We spent two years refusing to pick. V2 carries 10,000 mAh and still sits 17.4 mm low at the front. It reports 8,000 times a second when you want speed, and runs up to 1,000 hours when you would rather forget the cable. Every key lights up, and the price still starts at $99.
Big battery and low front. Fast and long-lived. Bright and $99. All of it, at once.
[画像: Engineered for longer battery life: 1,000 h on one charge (Bluetooth, lights off), 0.6 mW standby draw, per-key RGB lighting. A Venn diagram puts Rainy 75 V2 where a 10,000 mAh big battery, 8,000 Hz fast polling and a 17.4 mm low front overlap. Below, an illustrative see-through diagram shows the two battery cells, USB-C, a magnetic pogo-pin connection, a dedicated LED power rail, power-optimized 2.4 GHz, a low-power MCU with multi-stage sleep, and low-loss power components.]
[画像: YOU'LL WANT THE NEXT KEYSTROKE]
[画像: Animation: Rainy 75 V2 in moody blue light, moving from a low side view of the case to the back, where the USB-C port and power switch sit under the Rainy logo.]
First the sound. Two switch housings: Thock, deep and round; Clack, bright and short. Pick one, or both if you want.
Then the feel. Three gasket mounts, soft, even and firm, that swap without tools.
Under all of it, foams, rebuilt: six layers instead of five, so what reaches your ear is the key and nothing else. You will do this for years. Every keystroke should be one you look forward to.
Hear the sound test:
256 keyboards in one case.
Three gasket mounts, six foam layers, two switches. That is 256 ways to build one keyboard, or 512 if you own both switches. One press opens the case, every switch is hot-swap, and nothing needs solder or a screwdriver. Finding your sound takes minutes, not a weekend.
[画像: Animation: close-up of the plate's front edge under frosted keycaps as the gasket mount changes between the three silicone options.]
[画像: Formula: 4 gasket setups × 64 foam-layer combinations, × 2 for Deep or Crisp, = 256 (512) sounds.]
[画像: Animation titled SILICONE GASKET: three close-ups labeled Socks, Sleeve and Bean. A finger presses a key on each to show how the plate flexes with each gasket mount.]
Three gasket mounts. Swap them by hand.
[画像: Animation: a hand presses the edge of a cream Rainy 75 V2 and lifts the top frame straight off, showing the ball-catch latches and the plate inside. No screws, no tools.]
One press and the case is open. No screws, no tools.
## Modules
[画像: THE CORNER IS YOURS. One or two keys out. Module in.]
[画像: Animation: the top-right corner of a frosted, backlit Rainy 75 V2 cycles through its setups: a color LCD screen, the screen showing an illustration, one key plus a knob, and the default two keys.]
[画像: ONE CORNER. FOUR WAYS. In the box: one key out, knob in. Map the 5-pin knob to whatever you like. Default, as it ships; knob, volume by default, long-press for LED brightness. Add-on: both keys out, screen in. Magnets snap each module in, pogo pins carry power and signal. Color LCD shows your own images and GIFs; dot matrix + knob shows your own pixel patterns.]
The top-right corner ships as two keys. Pull one, and the knob from the box takes its place. Hot-swap, like every switch on the board.
[画像: Animation: installing the knob. A switch puller lifts the switch out of the top-right corner, the encoder goes into the same hot-swap socket, its cover is set on top, and the silver knob cap is pushed on.]
Out of the box it is a volume dial. Press and hold, and the same dial sets the brightness of the keyboard's lights.
Then give it your own job. In WOBKEY Studio, turning left, turning right and pressing each take any key or shortcut you choose. Scroll a long page. Zoom a canvas. Scrub a timeline. Skip a track. Step back through undo. Whatever your hands do a hundred times a day, put it on the dial.
Want a screen instead? Pull both keys.
[画像: Close-up of the top-right module bay with the top case off: magnetic pogo-pin contacts and a lit socket beside blue-backlit keys, with a screen module and a dot-matrix knob module lying nearby.]
A screen module takes the whole corner. Magnets snap it into place. Pogo pins carry power and signal, so there is no cable to plug in.Two are available as add-ons: a color LCD that plays your own images and GIFs, and a dot-matrix display with its own knob that shows the pixel patterns you draw.
Give that corner a life of its own.
Put a favorite photo on the color LCD, or give a pixel pet a home above your keys. Plug in over USB, upload it from your browser, and close the tab. Your photo stays up. Your GIF keeps looping.
Give it a job. Or invent a new one.
With the provided public display protocol, you can build your own tools for the color LCD—from a visual cue when Codex finishes a task to something only you would think to put above your keys.
Here are a few ideas to get you started. What comes next is yours to create.
THE BACK IS YOURS TOO.
Turn V2 over. The rear panel is held by magnets. Press the button and it lifts off; set it back and it snaps home. No screws, no pry tool, no marks on the case.
[画像: Animation: a hand holds a cream Rainy 75 V2 upside down. With the rear panel off, the bare underside shows its release button; then the glass panel is pressed on and snaps into place, with the word Snap.]
Under it is a slot for the 2.4G receiver. The receiver travels inside the keyboard, so it can't fall out of your bag or stay behind on the desk.
[画像: Screenshot of the Rainy75 V2 glass backplate tool: a 3D Satin Blue keyboard with a sunset photo printed under glass on the rear panel. Side panel: 'Your photo, printed under glass', custom or standard keycaps, six color and finish options, Download print file, Replace photo.]
And the panel is a canvas. Open our backplate tool in your browser, drop in a photo, pick your colorway, and see it on your keyboard before anything is printed. Then order it: we send you a link, you upload your design and order details, and we print it and ship it to you.
We make custom badges the same way. Full steps will follow in a project update.
## Design & Finish
[画像: FINISHED LIKE A WATCH. Milled, blasted, polished, passed by hand. Made to be handed on, not replaced.]
[画像: Side profile of Rainy 75 V2 on black, light catching the curved, CNC-milled waistline of the aluminum case under frosted keycaps.]
'The fact is the sweetest dream that labor knows.'
— Robert Frost, Mowing
A world of care. In every grain.
The dream was a $99 keyboard finished like a watch. The fact is in your hands: a block of aluminum, milled; fine beads at 220-mesh, thousands a second, until the surface is one even satin, a grain the width of a hair, no tool mark left anywhere; a rear panel polished by hand. Run a fingertip along the case. Dreams are cheap. This one weighs 1,535 grams.
[画像: TWELVE WAYS TO WANT IT. Six new colorways. Six V1 classics. Pick one.]
Five case colors, eight colorways, twelve SKUs: the same aluminum under every one, so the only decision left is the one you want to look at every day.
[画像: The 12 Rainy 75 V2 variants. New V2 keycaps: Mithril (Crisp: Cocoa V2 switch, FR4 plate), Smoke Black (Crisp), Pastel Cream (Deep: Mango V2 switch, PC plate), Mithril (Deep), Satin Blue (Deep), Frosted Rose (Deep, Mango V2 Pink switch). Classic V1 keycaps: Silver, Black and Cream, each in Crisp or Deep. Keycaps: 5-side dye-sub PBT, frosted shine-through, or double-shot PBT. One price: MSRP $169, from $99 on Kickstarter. Colorways shown are 3D renders.]
[画像: MORE KEYBOARD. LESS PAGE. Fifteen changes, one scroll, the full sheet below. The keyboard part ends here. Every number is one tap away, or at the very bottom.]
[画像: FULL SPEC SHEET: every number, every material, every layout, on one page. IT IS AT THE BOTTOM: prefer to scroll? The same sheet closes this page.]
## Reviews
[画像: NOT OUR WORDS. MKBHD, Hipyo Tech, WIRED, Forbes, Cult of Mac. MKBHD put it in front of 21.4 million people.]
[画像: THEY TYPED ON V2 FIRST. Creator quotes. gkey: 'Never thought there could be a more thocky keyboard than the original rainy75 but I've been proven wrong.' MightyAims: 'one of the few that made my jaw drop.' Code to the Moon: 'extend my compliments to the design/engineering team.' Tech Enthusiast: 'currently my favourite.' Saibot PC: 'absolutely impressed!' MechWhisper: 'a really awesome upgrade over the v1.' Lunatix Studio: 'i love it! the unboxing experience was top notch.']
@gkey64 · @MightyAims · @codetothemoom · @TechEnthusiastOfficial · @SaibotPC · @MechWhisper · @lunatixstudio
## Shows & Meetups
[画像: WE CAME TO YOU. 10+ shows, 10+ cities, 2024–2026. We took the keyboard to every show we could reach, so more people could see it before they bought it.]
[画像: WOBKEY booths with keyboards on display and visitors typing, in five photos: Tokyo Game Show, Japan, 2026; Tokyo Game Show, 2025; ZF, Akihabara, 2025; Tokyo Game Show, 2025; Tokyo Game Show, 2026.]
## In Stores
[画像: LANDED IN AKIHABARA. About 300 stores in Japan, Micro Center in the US. Yodobashi Akiba gave WOBKEY a section of its own.]
[画像: Rainy 75 in stores, in five photos: a WOBKEY wall at Yodobashi Camera, Akihabara, Tokyo; Yushakobo, Akihabara; Bic Camera, Ueno, with a shopper trying one; WOBKEY boxes on Micro Center shelves in the USA; and a Micro Center partner plaque presented to WOBKEY, 2025.]
## Why This Price
[画像: MARGIN OUT. YOU IN. $99, margin near nothing, shipping below cost. Yes, we profit from this, and we chose to profit less.]
[画像: $99 starting price, the same $99 as 2024, plus shipping from $15. Below what it costs us. The real rate is higher.]
[画像: Where your $99 goes: a bar splits the price into parts (aluminum case, PCB and chips, screen and knob, batteries, switches, plate and foam, keycaps, misc) up to $67, then assembly, QC, packaging, fees and a thin red margin up to $99. Below left: every part laid flat, about $67. Below right: global aluminum price (London Metal Exchange) rising from $2.3k in 2023 to $3.3k in 2026.]
…(以下省略)
risks: We plan to begin shipping in January 2027 and aim to complete deliveries by February 2027. Production, quality-control, customs, or carrier delays may affect this schedule. We will communicate any changes through project updates. If a parcel is confirmed lost in transit, we will arrange a replacement.
